title: Bilim

each / every, both / either / neither, most / most of

lessons.title: Genel olarak konuşmak
lessons.goal: Genelleme yaparken sıfır article, a / an ve the + tekil isim arasındaki farkı kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Arılar neden önemli?
discover.body:
Bees are among the most important animals on the planet. Without them, we would lose many of the fruits and vegetables we eat every day.

The honeybee, in particular, is a remarkable insect. A single bee visits up to several thousand flowers a day, and a colony can contain tens of thousands of bees.

But bees are in danger. Pesticides, disease and the loss of wild flowers have all played a part. Scientists say that protecting bees is not just about honey. It is about food security for the whole world.

The good news is that everyone can help. Planting flowers on a balcony or in a garden gives bees food and shelter.

options: Without them we would lose many fruits and vegetables.
questions.explanation: "we would lose many of the fruits and vegetables"
"Planting flowers on a balcony or in a garden"

learn.explanation:
Bir şey hakkında **genel olarak** (o türün hepsi hakkında) konuşmanın üç yolu var:

| Yapı | Örnek | Kullanım |
|---|---|---|
| **Sıfır article + çoğul** | **Bees** are important. | En yaygın, günlük dil |
| **Sıfır article + sayılamaz** | **Water** boils at 100°C. / **Research** shows ... | Sayılamaz isimler |
| **the + tekil** | **The honeybee** is a remarkable insect. | Daha resmî, bilimsel: tür, buluş, müzik aleti |
| **a / an + tekil** | **A** bee visits many flowers. | "Herhangi bir" örnek üzerinden |

**the + tekil isim** özellikle şunlar için kullanılır:

- **Hayvan / bitki türleri:** *The tiger is in danger.*
- **Buluşlar:** ***The telephone** was invented in the 19th century.*
- **Müzik aletleri:** *She plays **the** violin.*
- **Vücut organları (genel):** ***The heart** pumps blood.*

**En sık hata: genellemede "the" kullanmak**

- ~~**The** bees are important.~~ → **Bees** are important. (Genel)
- ~~**The** science is interesting.~~ → **Science** is interesting.
- ~~I love **the** music.~~ → I love **music**. (Genel)
- Ama: I love **the music** in this film. (Belirli)

examples.en: Vaccines save millions of lives every year.
examples.tr: Aşılar her yıl milyonlarca hayat kurtarıyor.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede article olmadığı için "Arılar önemlidir" ve "Bu arılar önemli" arasındaki fark bağlamla anlaşılır. İngilizcede genel konuşurken çoğul ve sayılamaz isimlerin önüne "the" konmaz. Türkçe konuşanların en sık hatası "The people are...", "The life is..." gibi genellemelerdir. Doğrusu "People are...", "Life is...".

task.modelAnswer: Elephants are my favourite animals. The African elephant is the largest land animal in the world, and elephants can remember other elephants for many years. The bicycle is one of the best inventions ever. It was invented in the 19th century, and bicycles are still the cheapest and healthiest way to travel in a city. I find biology fascinating. Biology explains how life works, from cells to whole ecosystems.

lessons.title: The ne zaman gelir?
lessons.goal: Özel isimler, kurumlar ve coğrafi adlarla the kullanımının kurallarını uygulayabilirim.

discover.title: Bir bilim insanının hayatı
discover.body:
Aziz Sancar was born in 1946 in Savur, a small town in Mardin. He studied medicine at Istanbul University and worked as a doctor for a short time before moving to the United States.

He did his PhD at the University of Texas and later became a professor at the University of North Carolina, where he still works today.

In 2015, he won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, together with Tomas Lindahl from Sweden and Paul Modrich from the USA, for their work on how cells repair damaged DNA. His research helps scientists understand diseases such as cancer.

After the prize, he gave his Nobel medal to Anıtkabir in Ankara as a gift to the Turkish people.

questions.prompt: Where did Aziz Sancar study medicine?
What was his Nobel Prize for?

learn.explanation:
**Coğrafi adlar:**

| the KULLANILIR | the KULLANILMAZ |
|---|---|
| Okyanus, deniz, nehir: **the** Pacific, **the** Black Sea, **the** Nile | Göl: Lake Van |
| Dağ sıraları: **the** Alps, **the** Taurus Mountains | Tek dağ: Mount Ararat (Ağrı Dağı) |
| Çoğul ülkeler, "States/Kingdom/Republic": **the** USA, **the** UK, **the** Netherlands, **the** Philippines | Çoğu ülke, şehir, kıta: Turkey, Ankara, Asia |
| Çöller: **the** Sahara | |

**Kurumlar ve yerler:**

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **University of / of** yapısı → the | **the** University of Texas, **the** Museum of Modern Art |
| İsimle başlayan → the yok | Istanbul University, Harvard University |

**Kurum işlevi için the yok:**

| the YOK (amacına uygun) | the VAR (bina olarak) |
|---|---|
| She's **in hospital**. (hasta) | I visited her at **the hospital**. |
| He went **to prison**. (mahkûm) | His mum went to **the prison** to see him. |
| I'm **at school / university**. (öğrenci) | The meeting is at **the school**. |

**Hastalıklar:** Çoğunlukla article yok: *cancer, diabetes, flu* (ama *a cold, a headache*)

**Benzersiz şeyler:** **the** sun, **the** moon, **the** Earth (ama *on Earth*), **the** internet

examples.en: The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
My grandmother is in hospital with pneumonia.
She did her PhD at the University of Oxford.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "hastanede" hem "hasta olarak yatıyor" hem de "hastane binasında" anlamına gelebilir. İngilizcede bu fark article ile yapılır: "in hospital" (hasta), "at the hospital" (ziyaretçi, çalışan). Ülke adlarında da dikkat: "the Turkey" yanlıştır; ama "the United States" ve "the Netherlands" doğrudur.

options: My mum is in the hospital building.

task.prompt: Türkiye'den ya da dünyadan bir bilim insanının, bir sporcunun ya da bir sanatçının hayatını anlatın. Doğduğu yer, okuduğu kurumlar (the University of ... / ... University), gittiği ülkeler (the USA, Germany), coğrafi yerler (the Mediterranean, Lake ..., Mount ...) gibi en az 6 özel isim kullanın ve article'lara dikkat edin.
task.modelAnswer: Cahit Arf was one of Turkey's greatest mathematicians. He was born in Thessaloniki in 1910, and his family later moved to Izmir. He studied in France and then did his PhD at the University of Göttingen in Germany. Later, he taught at Istanbul University and spent time at the Institute for Advanced Study in the USA. One of his discoveries is named after him: the Arf invariant. His picture was even on the 10 lira note.

learn.explanation:
**a few / few** (sayılabilir) ve **a little / little** (sayılamaz)

| Yapı | Anlam | Ton |
|---|---|---|
| **a few** people | birkaç kişi | olumlu: **yeterli** |
| **few** people | çok az kişi | olumsuz: **yetersiz** |
| **a little** time | biraz zaman | olumlu: **yeterli** |
| **little** time | çok az zaman | olumsuz: **yetersiz** |

- *I have **a few** friends here.* (Birkaç arkadaşım var, yalnız değilim.)
- *I have **few** friends here.* (Çok az arkadaşım var, yalnızım.)
- ***Little** is known about this disease.* (Hakkında çok az şey biliniyor.)

**Bol miktar:**

| Yapı | İsim türü | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **plenty of** | ikisi de | plenty of **water** / plenty of **ideas** |
| **a lot of / lots of** | ikisi de | a lot of **research** |
| **a great deal of** | sayılamaz (resmî) | a great deal of **evidence** |
| **a large number of** | sayılabilir (resmî) | a large number of **patients** |
| **a large amount of** | sayılamaz (resmî) | a large amount of **data** |

**Çok az / hiç:**

- **hardly any** = neredeyse hiç: *There's **hardly any** sugar left.*
- **very few / very little** = çok az
- **no / none** = hiç

examples.en: Few people know that the brain has no pain receptors.

examples.en: There is a great deal of evidence that smoking causes cancer.

examples.en: I had a little time, so I read the article.
examples.tr: Biraz vaktim vardı, o yüzden makaleyi okudum.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "birkaç" ile "çok az" arasındaki fark kelime seçimiyle yapılır; İngilizcede bu fark sadece "a" ile belirlenir: a few (birkaç, yeterli) / few (çok az, yetersiz). Bu küçük kelime cümlenin tonunu tamamen değiştirir. "a great deal of" sadece sayılamaz isimlerle kullanılır: "a great deal of people" yanlıştır; "a large number of people" doğrudur.

lessons.title: Her biri, ikisi de, hiçbiri
lessons.goal: each / every, both / either / neither, all / none ve most / most of yapılarını doğru kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Bir ilaç denemesi
discover.body:
In a recent study, 400 patients with high blood pressure were divided into two groups. Each group received a different treatment for six months.

The first group took a new drug, and the second group took a placebo (a pill with no medicine in it). Every participant also followed the same diet and exercise plan.

By the end of the study, most of the patients in the first group had lower blood pressure. Interestingly, some of the patients in the second group also improved, probably because of the diet and exercise.

Both groups reported a few minor side effects, but neither group had any serious problems. None of the participants left the study early.

The researchers say that both the drug and lifestyle changes are important, and that either one alone may not be enough for most people.

questions.prompt: What did the second group take?

questions.explanation: "None of the participants left the study early."

learn.explanation:
**each / every**

| | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **each** | her biri (ayrı ayrı, 2 ve üstü) | **Each** group received a different treatment. |
| **every** | her (hepsi bir arada, 3 ve üstü) | **Every** participant followed the diet. |

İkisi de **tekil isim + tekil fiil** alır: *Every patient **was** ...*

**İki şey için: both / either / neither**

| Yapı | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **both** (of) | ikisi de | **Both** groups improved. / **Both of** them ... |
| **either** (of) | ikisinden biri | You can take **either** pill. |
| **neither** (of) | ikisi de değil | **Neither** group had problems. |
| **both ... and** | hem ... hem | **both** the drug **and** exercise |
| **either ... or** | ya ... ya | **either** today **or** tomorrow |
| **neither ... nor** | ne ... ne | **neither** sugar **nor** salt |

**most / most of**

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **most** + isim (genel) | **Most people** like chocolate. |
| **most of the / my / these** + isim (belirli) | **Most of the patients** in the study improved. |
| ~~most of people~~ ✗ | |

**all / none:** *All (of) the participants ... / **None of** the participants ...*

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "insanların çoğu" dediğimiz için "most of people" demek doğal gelir, ama bu yanlıştır. Genel konuşurken "most people", belirli bir grup için "most of the people" kullanılır. Ayrıca "Her iki grup da" demek için "both groups", "İki grup da ... değildi" demek için "neither group" kullanılır; "both groups didn't" pek doğal değildir.

lessons.title: Bulguları aktarmak
lessons.goal: Bir araştırmanın bulgularını doğru article ve miktar ifadeleriyle özetleyen popüler bilim metni yazabilirim.

discover.title: Popüler bilim: Uyku ve ekranlar
discover.body:
Do you check your phone in bed? You're not alone, and it may be affecting your sleep.

A recent study of 2,000 university students found that the majority of participants used a screen in the hour before bed. Nearly a third said they used their phones for more than an hour after turning off the lights.

The researchers found a significant link between screen use and sleep quality. Students who used screens late at night slept, on average, 45 minutes less than those who didn't. They were also twice as likely to feel tired during the day.

However, only a small minority of participants believed that their phones affected their sleep.

The good news is that small changes can make a big difference. When a group of students stopped using screens an hour before bed for two weeks, most of them reported sleeping better.

The researchers point out that the study had some limitations. All of the participants were students, so the findings may not apply to everyone.

questions.prompt: How much less did late screen users sleep on average?
What is one limitation of the study?

learn.explanation:
**Araştırma bulgularını aktarma dili:**

| İşlev | Kalıplar |
|---|---|
| **Çalışmayı tanıtma** | *A recent study of 2,000 adults found that ...* / *Researchers at ... have discovered that ...* |
| **Oranlar** | *the majority of* (çoğunluğu), *a minority of* (azınlığı), *nearly half*, *a third of*, *one in five*, *over 60%* |
| **Karşılaştırma** | *twice as likely to* (iki kat daha fazla olası), *significantly more / less* |
| **İlişki** | *a link between X and Y* / *X is associated with Y* |
| **Dikkatli yorum** | *suggests that* / *may be linked to* / *it appears that* |
| **Sınırlılık** | *The study had some limitations.* / *The findings may not apply to ...* / *More research is needed.* |

**Oran ve fiil uyumu:**

- *The majority of **participants were** ...* (çoğul isim → çoğul fiil)
- *A third of **the money was** ...* (sayılamaz → tekil fiil)
- *One in five **people has / have** ...* (ikisi de kabul edilir)

**Bağlantı ≠ neden:** *Screen use **is linked to** poor sleep.* (Bağlantılı, ama sebep olduğu kanıtlanmadı.) Popüler bilim yazarken bu farka dikkat edin.

examples.en: The majority of participants reported feeling better.
examples.tr: Katılımcıların çoğunluğu daha iyi hissettiğini bildirdi.

examples.en: Smokers are twice as likely to develop heart disease.
examples.tr: Sigara içenlerin kalp hastalığına yakalanma olasılığı iki kat daha fazla.

examples.tr: Bulgular daha fazla araştırmaya ihtiyaç olduğunu gösteriyor.

learn.turkishNote: Türk basınında "Bilim insanları kanıtladı: Kahve kanseri önlüyor!" gibi başlıklar sık görülür. İyi bir İngilizce popüler bilim yazısı ise daha temkinlidir: "proves" yerine "suggests", "causes" yerine "is linked to" kullanır. Bu temkinli dili C1'de daha ayrıntılı göreceksiniz (hedging). Oranlarda da Türkçedeki "üçte biri" İngilizcede "a third of" olur; "one third of" da kullanılabilir.

options: Screen use is linked to poor sleep.

task.prompt: Bir popüler bilim dergisi için hayali bir araştırmanın bulgularını aktaran kısa bir makale yazın (180–220 kelime). Konu seçenekleri: kahve ve hafıza, yürüyüş ve mutluluk, müzik ve çalışma verimi. Okuyucunun ilgisini çeken bir giriş, oranlar (the majority of, a third of, one in five), karşılaştırma (twice as likely), temkinli yorum (suggests, is linked to) ve bir sınırlılık cümlesi kullanın. Article ve miktar ifadelerine dikkat edin.
task.modelAnswer:
Need a mood boost? Try going for a walk.

A new study of 1,500 office workers suggests that a short daily walk may have a significant effect on happiness. The participants were divided into two groups. Each person in the first group walked for 20 minutes every day for eight weeks, while the second group continued their normal routine.

By the end of the study, the majority of walkers said they felt happier and less stressed. Nearly a third reported sleeping better, and one in five said they had more energy at work. In contrast, very few people in the second group noticed any change.

The researchers also found that walkers were twice as likely to describe their mood as "good" or "very good". Interestingly, the benefits were greatest for people who walked outdoors, especially in parks or near water.

However, the study had some limitations. All of the participants worked in offices in large cities, so the findings may not apply to everyone. The researchers also point out that walking is linked to better mood, but it may not be the only reason for it.

Still, the message is simple: a little exercise goes a long way.

questions.modelAnswer:
Few discoveries have saved as many lives as penicillin, and it all happened by accident.

In 1928, Alexander Fleming, a Scottish scientist working at St Mary's Hospital in London, returned from a holiday and noticed something strange. A mould had grown on one of his dishes of bacteria, and the bacteria around it had died. Fleming realised that the mould was producing a substance that could kill bacteria. He called it penicillin.

At first, however, little attention was paid to his discovery. It was very difficult to produce penicillin in large amounts, and few scientists believed it would be useful. It wasn't until the 1940s that a team at the University of Oxford found a way to produce it on a larger scale.

During the Second World War, penicillin saved a large number of soldiers' lives. Since then, antibiotics have become one of the most important tools in medicine. Most of the infections that once killed people can now be treated in a few days.

But there is a problem. Bacteria are becoming resistant to antibiotics, and neither doctors nor patients always use them carefully. Scientists warn that if we don't act, the majority of today's antibiotics may stop working.

Fleming himself warned about this in 1945. Perhaps it's time we listened.
